Q1.problem_type_and_essence: precedence-constrained permutation/scheduling to minimize peak live-buffer residency

author_route.method: multi-initialization (FREE-first / DFS / critical-path) + topology-preserving simulated annealing
why_fit: multiple cheap initializers exploit graph structure before metaheuristic refinement
author_route.evidence_boundary: SA is paper-described but its main loop is not visible in printed Q1.py

baseline.name: FREE-first + critical-path tie-break list scheduling
six_hour_plan: ready queue prioritizes FREE, then high critical-path height, then small ALLOC size
baseline.why: simple, deterministic, topology-safe, O((N+E)logN), gives a credible benchmark before metaheuristics

major_alternatives.why_can_work: directly encodes precedence and peak-residency objective
major_alternatives.when_prefer: small/medium graphs or when optimality gap is valuable
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: Conv_Case1/Matmul_Case1 scale makes O(N^2) position binaries expensive

major_alternatives.model: beam search / bounded best-first topological scheduling
major_alternatives.why_can_work: keeps several promising ready-set choices and provides an anytime quality/runtime trade-off
major_alternatives.when_prefer: medium graphs with stronger runtime budget than greedy but less than SA
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: state branching can explode and needs a good admissible/lower-bound heuristic

major_alternatives.when_prefer: diverse repeated graph families and generous tuning budget
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: higher tuning cost than SA and easy to generate infeasible permutations if operators are not DAG-aware

not_recommended.reason: no supervised target dataset for optimal schedules; sequence modeling does not solve precedence-constrained search by itself
needs many simulator episodes and repeated problem distribution; unnecessary before a strong deterministic baseline on six fixed instances

switch_conditions: use CP-SAT/MILP if graph is small enough to obtain optimum/gap within contest time
use SA/beam search only if matched-budget validation shows material peak reduction over deterministic baseline
abandon metaheuristic if improvement is unstable or runtime dominates schedule-evaluation budget

Q2.problem_type_and_essence: lifetime-aware multi-cache address allocation with capacity/non-overlap constraints and spill-cost minimization

target_and_constraints.objective: min total extra data movement from SPILL

author_route.method: colored-edge graph + paper-claimed ILP/LP-rounding hybrid + hierarchical allocator + SPILL victim heuristic
why_fit: lifetime overlap resembles register allocation/interference coloring
small instances admit exact resource allocation
large instances need fast repair/spill heuristic
author_route.evidence_boundary: printed Q2.py exposes heuristic allocation/SPILL, not visible ILP/CBC model or solve call

baseline.name: per-cache linear-scan/Best-Fit allocator + lifecycle intervals + greedy spill
six_hour_plan: maintain free blocks per cache type
baseline.why: fully executable, easy to audit, directly exposes fragmentation and spill cost

major_alternatives.when_prefer: small graphs or for exact lower bounds on selected subinstances
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: full large instances may exceed solver budget

major_alternatives.why_can_work: lifetime overlap naturally maps to conflict graph
major_alternatives.when_prefer: many overlapping lifetimes with discrete cache slots/regions
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: variable buffer sizes and continuous offsets require weighted/interval extensions

major_alternatives.why_can_work: can represent movement/reuse costs in structured time-expanded cases
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when cache slots can be discretized and transitions dominate
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: continuous address packing and size heterogeneity make graph expansion large

not_recommended.reason: no large labeled optimum corpus, hard feasibility must be guaranteed, and deterministic heuristics are easier to validate

switch_conditions: invoke exact solver only on tractable subgraphs or time-limited exact path
reject any heuristic mapping that fails post-repair feasibility replay
centralize victim policy before composing Q2 and Q3

Q3.problem_type_and_essence: heterogeneous-pipeline scheduling under a hard transfer-cost cap; minimize makespan while preserving feasible cache allocation

author_route.method: adaptive priority scheduling + time-sensitive Best-Fit + constrained multi-objective/local search narrative
why_fit: execution time depends on critical path and pipe contention
hard transfer budget is naturally an epsilon constraint
author_route.evidence_boundary: printed Q3.py does not expose the claimed adaptive-priority/Best-Fit/Pareto/2-opt loop; Table 5.5 contains infeasible rows

baseline.name: epsilon-constraint list scheduling
six_hour_plan: take Q2 feasible allocation/cost as baseline
critical-path list scheduler with pipe availability
Best-Fit allocation with exact same victim registry
select minimum T among feasible candidates
baseline.why: matches the actual hard constraint, avoids arbitrary unit-mixing scalarization, and is auditable

major_alternatives.model: NSGA-II / Pareto search with feasibility-first ranking
major_alternatives.why_can_work: explores time-transfer trade-off and can return a nondominated set
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when organizers/decision maker wants several trade-off operating points
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: hard 1.05 cap already defines a natural epsilon constraint; extra Pareto machinery is useful only if feasible diversity exists

major_alternatives.model: MILP/CP-SAT joint scheduling for small instances
major_alternatives.why_can_work: can jointly encode precedence, pipe disjunctions and transfer cap
major_alternatives.when_prefer: small cases/benchmark subgraphs to establish quality gaps
metrics are normalized and preference weight is justified
major_alternatives.why_not_primary_here: fixed mu mixes cycles and bytes without a demonstrated scale/preference contract

not_recommended.reason: six fixed graphs do not supply the repeated training distribution needed to justify RL; feasibility and simulator fidelity dominate risk
unit/preference ambiguity and can accept hard-cap violations unless feasibility is enforced first

switch_conditions: if exact small-instance solve shows large gap, invest in richer search
if no candidate improves T under 1.05 cap, keep Q2 baseline and explicitly report no feasible improvement
if workload family behavior differs, use workload-specific policy selection rather than one universal heuristic
